title: "Kaplan–Meier survival curves in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Turn a survival table into an interactive, reproducible Kaplan–Meier plot stratified by treatment arm — with censoring ticks — in a few lines of browser JavaScript."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"
date: "2026-09-21"
categories: [JavaScript, CanvasXpress, survival, bioinformatics, visualization]
image: "thumbnail.png"
---

Kaplan–Meier curves summarize time-to-event data: the step-down survival probability over time,
usually split by a group like treatment arm. CanvasXpress computes the survival steps for you — you
give it a **time** column and a **censoring** column — so in the browser it's just a `data` object
and a `config`. The result is interactive and reproducible.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

Subjects are the variables (rows); each row holds `[Time, Time-Censor]` (1 = censored, 0 = event).
The arm rides along as a variable annotation. The key is `graphType: "KaplanMeier"` and passing
**both** columns to `xAxis`.

```html
<canvas id="km" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  var subj = [], rows = [], arm = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
    var a = Math.random() < 0.5 ? "Treatment" : "Control";
    var base = a === "Treatment" ? 60 : 40;                 // treatment survives longer
    var time = Math.round(-base * Math.log(Math.random()) * 10) / 10;  // exponential
    var cens = Math.random() < 0.3 ? 1 : 0;                 // 1 = censored, 0 = event
    subj.push("Subj" + (i + 1));
    rows.push([time, cens]);
    arm.push(a);
  }

  var data = {
    y: { vars: subj, smps: ["Time", "Time-Censor"], data: rows },
    z: { Arm: arm }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "KaplanMeier",
    xAxis: ["Time", "Time-Censor"],
    colorBy: "Arm",
    title: "Overall survival by treatment arm",
    xAxisTitle: "Time (weeks)", yAxisTitle: "Probability of survival",
    invertCensored: true,                 // draw censoring ticks
    showKMConfidenceIntervals: false
  };

  new CanvasXpress("km", data, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="kmLive" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var subj = [], rows = [], arm = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      var a = Math.random() < 0.5 ? "Treatment" : "Control";
      var base = a === "Treatment" ? 60 : 40;
      var time = Math.round(-base * Math.log(Math.random()) * 10) / 10;
      var cens = Math.random() < 0.3 ? 1 : 0;
      subj.push("Subj" + (i + 1));
      rows.push([time, cens]);
      arm.push(a);
    }
    new CanvasXpress("kmLive",
      { y: { vars: subj, smps: ["Time", "Time-Censor"], data: rows }, z: { Arm: arm } },
      { graphType: "KaplanMeier", xAxis: ["Time", "Time-Censor"], colorBy: "Arm",
        title: "Overall survival by treatment arm",
        xAxisTitle: "Time (weeks)", yAxisTitle: "Probability of survival",
        invertCensored: true, showKMConfidenceIntervals: false });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Hover any step for the time and survival probability; the tick marks are censored subjects.
CanvasXpress derives the survival curve from the raw table, so you never precompute the steps — and
the same spec re-renders the identical curve from R or Python.

## A common gotcha

The survival transform only fires with `graphType: "KaplanMeier"`. A bare `"Scatter2D"` gives a raw
scatter of the censor values instead — survival probability is *computed* by the engine, not a
column in your data.
